title: What knowledge and competence does the Mortgage Credit Directive require of mortgage staff?
description: What Article 9 and Annex III of the EU Mortgage Credit Directive require of lender and broker staff, who counts as staff, and how to evidence competence.
shortAnswer: Article 9 of the Mortgage Credit Directive (Directive 2014/17/EU) requires creditors, credit intermediaries and appointed representatives to ensure their staff possess and keep up to date an appropriate level of knowledge and competence for residential mortgage lending, intermediation and advice. Annex III lists nine minimum knowledge areas, and home Member States set the detailed requirements. Since March 21, 2019, competence cannot be determined on professional experience alone.
keyTakeaways: Article 9(1) puts the duty on the firm: creditors, credit intermediaries and appointed representatives must require their staff to possess and keep up to date appropriate knowledge and competence.
Annex III sets nine minimum areas, from credit products and consumer protection law to security valuation, land registers, business ethics and creditworthiness assessment.

Member States determine the level through professional qualifications (diplomas, degrees, training, competency tests) or professional experience, but after March 21, 2019 experience alone is not enough.
Competent authorities supervise compliance and can require firms to provide whatever evidence they deem necessary (Article 9(4)).
The new Consumer Credit Directive, (EU) 2023/2225, applies a parallel staff competence duty to consumer credit from November 20, 2026.
regulator: National competent authorities designated by each Member State under Article 5 of Directive 2014/17/EU, within the framework set by the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union
appliesTo: Creditors granting credit agreements for residential immovable property to consumers
Credit intermediaries and appointed representatives carrying out credit intermediation or advisory services
Front office and back office staff directly engaged in the credit agreement process, including management and outsourced personnel
Persons managing credit intermediaries or appointed representatives (Article 29(2)(c) and Article 31(2))

sections.heading: What does Article 9 of the Mortgage Credit Directive require?

blocks.text: Article 9 requires Member States to ensure that creditors, credit intermediaries and appointed representatives require their staff to possess, and keep up to date, an appropriate level of knowledge and competence. The duty covers the manufacturing, offering or granting of credit agreements, credit intermediation activities and advisory services, and extends to any ancillary service bundled with the credit agreement.

blocks.title: Article 9(1), Directive 2014/17/EU
blocks.text: "Member States shall ensure that creditors, credit intermediaries and appointed representatives require their staff to possess and to keep up-to-date an appropriate level of knowledge and competence in relation to the manufacturing, the offering or granting of credit agreements, the carrying out of credit intermediation activities set out in point 5 of Article 4 or the provision of advisory services."

The Directive is a minimum framework. Article 9(2) requires the home Member State to establish minimum knowledge and competence requirements "in accordance with the principles set out in Annex III", so the detailed rules a firm must meet sit in national law. Article 9(4) requires competent authorities to supervise compliance and gives them power to require "such evidence as the competent authority deems necessary" ([Directive 2014/17/EU on EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32014L0017)). As at November 2026, Article 9 and Annex III have not been amended since adoption.

Recital 32 explains the design choice: knowledge and competence is to be proven "at the level of the company", while Member States remain free to impose individual requirements on natural persons. That is why some countries run individual certification schemes and others rely on firm level assurance. The Portuguese implementation is covered in [credit intermediary training requirements in Portugal](/regulations/portugal-credit-intermediaries-training-requirements).

sections.heading: Who counts as staff under the Directive?

blocks.text: Staff means people who work on the credit agreement process or deal with consumers, plus the people who directly manage or supervise them. Article 4(10) defines staff as any natural person working for a creditor or credit intermediary who is directly engaged in activities covered by the Directive or has contact with consumers in that context, any natural person working for an appointed representative who has contact with consumers, and any natural person directly managing or supervising those people.
Recital 32 adds three clarifications that shape the scope of a training program:

items: **Outsourced personnel count.** Staff includes outsourced personnel working for and within the creditor, credit intermediary or appointed representative, as well as employees.

**Back office counts.** Staff directly engaged in activities under the Directive include both front office and back office staff, including management, who fulfill an important role in the credit agreement process.
**Unrelated support functions do not.** Human resources and information and communications technology personnel whose work is unrelated to the credit agreement process are not staff for this purpose.

blocks.text: Recital 32 also allows firms, where national law permits, to differentiate the level of required knowledge by each person's involvement in particular services or processes. A role based approach, documented in a [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix), is therefore consistent with the Directive's intent.

sections.heading: What are the nine minimum knowledge areas in Annex III?

blocks.text: Annex III, point 1, lists nine areas that minimum knowledge and competence requirements must include at least. They apply to staff under Article 9 and to persons involved in managing credit intermediaries or appointed representatives under Article 29(2)(c) and Article 31(2).

items: Appropriate knowledge of credit products within the scope of Article 3 and the ancillary services typically offered with them.
Appropriate knowledge of the laws related to credit agreements for consumers, in particular consumer protection.
Appropriate knowledge and understanding of the immovable property purchasing process.
Appropriate knowledge of the organization and functioning of land registers.
Appropriate knowledge of the market in the relevant Member State.
Appropriate knowledge of business ethics standards.
Appropriate knowledge of the consumer's creditworthiness assessment process or, where applicable, competence in assessing consumers' creditworthiness.
An appropriate level of financial and economic competency.

blocks.text: Annex III, point 2, lets Member States set different levels and types of requirement for creditor staff, intermediary or appointed representative staff, and the management of intermediaries or appointed representatives. Under Article 9(3), when a firm passports services under the freedom to provide services, the host Member State may set its own requirements for areas (b), (c), (e) and (f): consumer credit law, the property purchasing process, land registers and the local market. Branch staff follow host Member State requirements in full.

sections.heading: How must Member States determine whether staff are competent?

blocks.text: Member States must base the appropriate level of knowledge and competence on professional qualifications, professional experience, or both, and from March 21, 2019 experience alone is not sufficient. Annex III, point 3, names the two routes: professional qualifications ("e.g. diplomas, degrees, training, competency tests") or professional experience, defined as a minimum number of years working in credit origination, distribution or intermediation.

The final sentence of Annex III, point 3, closed the experience only route: "After 21 March 2019, the determination of the appropriate level of knowledge and competence shall not be based solely on the methods listed in point (b)". Long serving mortgage staff without a qualification therefore needed training, a competency test or a recognized diploma by that date under most national schemes. Member States had to transpose and apply the Directive from March 21, 2016 (Article 42).

sections.heading: How do the obligations map to roles, frequency and audit evidence?

blocks.text: Because Article 9(4) lets supervisors demand any evidence they consider necessary, a firm should be able to show, role by role, which Annex III areas each person has mastered, how that was verified and how it is kept current. The table below is an original, illustrative mapping. National rules set the binding detail, including any certification and refresh intervals, so it should be adjusted to the Member State concerned.

sections.heading: How does the new Consumer Credit Directive change things?

blocks.text: The revised Consumer Credit Directive, Directive (EU) 2023/2225, extends a near identical competence duty to consumer credit, with national measures applying from November 20, 2026. Article 33 requires creditors and credit intermediaries to require their staff to possess and keep up to date an appropriate level of knowledge and competence, including in relation to consumer rights in the area of their trade, and requires Member States to set minimum requirements ([Directive (EU) 2023/2225 on EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32023L2225)).

Unlike Annex III of the Mortgage Credit Directive, Article 33 does not list minimum knowledge areas, so national transposition will decide the content. Lenders that offer both mortgages and unsecured consumer credit should expect two overlapping competence regimes from late 2026 and can usually run a single competence framework with product specific modules. Transposition status varies by Member State as at November 2026.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models the nine Annex III areas, the national requirements layered on them, and each role's level of involvement as a structured framework before any course is written. Assessment points attach to each area, so a supervisor's evidence request can be answered by role and by person, and a change in lending policy or national rules shows which roles and assessments are affected.

faqs.q: Does the Mortgage Credit Directive require individual certification of every adviser?
faqs.a: No. Recital 32 says knowledge and competence is to be proven at the level of the company, while Member States may introduce or keep requirements applicable to individual natural persons. Whether an individual exam or certificate is mandatory therefore depends on the national rules of the Member State concerned.

faqs.q: Do IT and HR staff at a mortgage lender need MCD competence training?
faqs.a: Not under the Directive, unless their role is part of the credit agreement process. Recital 32 states that persons fulfilling support functions unrelated to the credit agreement process, such as human resources and information and communications technology personnel, should not be considered staff for this purpose.

faqs.q: Does the Directive set a minimum number of CPD hours?
faqs.a: No. Article 9 requires staff to keep their knowledge and competence up to date but sets no hours or refresh interval. Any hours, exam renewal cycle or continuing professional development requirement comes from national transposing law or the competent authority's rules.

faqs.q: Which country's rules apply when a broker passports into another Member State?
faqs.a: Under Article 9(3), branch staff follow host Member State requirements. Under the freedom to provide services, the home Member State sets the requirements, but the host may set its own for consumer credit law, the property purchasing process, land registers and the local market (Annex III points (b), (c), (e) and (f)).

factCheck.claim: Article 9(1) requires creditors, credit intermediaries and appointed representatives to require staff to possess and keep up to date appropriate knowledge and competence, including for ancillary services

Article 9(2) requires home Member States to set minimum requirements in accordance with Annex III; Article 9(3) splits home and host responsibility for branches and freedom to provide services, with host scope limited to Annex III points (b), (c), (e) and (f)
Article 9(4) requires competent authorities to supervise and gives them power to require evidence they deem necessary
Annex III point 1 lists nine minimum knowledge areas (a) to (i); point 2 allows differentiation; point 3 names qualifications or experience and bars reliance solely on experience after 21 March 2019
Article 4(10) definition of staff; Recital 32 on company level proof, outsourced personnel, front and back office, and exclusion of HR and ICT support functions
Article 42: transposition and application from 21 March 2016
Amendment history shows modifications by 2016/1011 and 2021/2167 (Articles 13, 27a, 28, 28a, 42, 43) and partial repeal of Article 46 by 2023/2225, with no change to Article 9 or Annex III
Directive (EU) 2023/2225 Article 33 sets a staff knowledge and competence duty for consumer credit; Article 48 requires measures to apply from 20 November 2026
